To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
for a large class of distributions, the seller can trade an indivisible object in a way that is ex post efficient and individually rational.
for a large class of probability distributions, a simple trading mechanism exists which is ex post efficient, individually rational and truthful.
for an open set of distributions, there exists an ex post efficient mechanism for trading a single indivisible object that is individually rational and that is a bidding game.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a problem that is similar to the standard auction problem, but with the difference that there is only one seller and at least two buyers.

the design of a mechanism for the trading of an indivisible good in a setting in which the seller′s valuation for the good is lower than the highest potential buyers′ valuations, but by an arbitrarily small margin.

the following question: What are the properties of a mechanism that will be used by a seller of an indivisable object to sell it in an auction to a set of buyers, when the buyers′ valuations are private information and the seller′s valuation is common knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the authors prove the existence of a mechanism for trading an indivisible object, which is ex post efficient and individually rational, for a family of probability distributions that is an open set in probability space.

the results of this paper show the possibility of a mechanism for trading an indivisible object in which the object is allocated in an ex-post efficient and individually rational way to one of two bidders.
the authors prove that there exist mechanisms that are individually rational, ex-post efficient and implementable as a simple bidding game for an open set of valuation distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that there are efficient mechanisms for trading an indivisible object, when the seller and the buyers are risk neutral, the buyers have private valuations, the highest buyer′s valuation is greater than the seller′ s, and the valuations of the buyers are independent.
we have found an open set of distributions for which there is a simple, efficient, Bayesian mechanism.
, for a large family of distributions, there exist efficient mechanisms which are simple to compute, and simple to implement by the players.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there exist mechanisms that satisfy the desirable properties of ex post efficiency and individual rationality.
the possibility of an ex post efficient outcome in a trading problem does not depend on the assumption that the traders′ valuations are common knowledge.
the possibility of an efficient trading mechanism is not a function of the distribution of the valuations, but rather a function of the structure of the valuations.
